turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Come on in, I'm the one who checked him in. Weight's thirty-one pounds, temp ninety-eight point four, pulse one eighteen. He fussed the whole time out front.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks. Sorry we blew in late, the rain had the 405 just crawling.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I know, I sat forever at that off-ramp. Garage give you any trouble?
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Third level, then the elevator that smells like a wet dog. We almost did the stairs with the stroller.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): That elevator's been rank all week, maintenance keeps saying tomorrow. Doctor's finishing a note, she'll be right in.
[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Fine. He's wiped. Oh, random, but that dinosaur shirt is from my nephew's birthday last month, bounce place on Lincoln, total circus, cake in everybody's hair.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Ha, those places are chaos. Alright, I'll let her know you're here.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm Dr. Shah. What brings him in?
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Leo's ear. He's three. Been crying at night and grabbing the right one, started after this cold.
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): Ear hurt. No.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right side only?
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, the right. He won't let me near it.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has the night crying been going on?
[SEG0014] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two nights. Um, the cold's been, what, almost a week. Runny nose, and a little cough.
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): Mommy.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I felt him, he wasn't hot, and I didn't even bother with the thermometer.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting? Anything draining from the ear?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No throwing up. No gunk coming out.
[SEG0020] person_4 (PATIENT): Stop.

[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, actually, hold on. My mom had him yesterday afternoon and she said he felt hot, like really warm. She never took a temperature though. I still don't think it was a fever.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Drinking?
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, juice and milk. He's just cranky.
[SEG0024] person_4 (PATIENT): Juice!
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Daycare?
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Little Oaks, three mornings. They called me yesterday 'cause he was crying, so I picked him up. Not sick-sick, just miserable.

[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And this is dumb, but his dad texted me in the car to ask if Leo could catch his sugar thing. He's been living on his metformin. I told him no, that's not how it works, right?
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, that's your husband's medicine, not Leo's. What has Leo actually taken?
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The bubblegum Tylenol. Kids' one. I gave maybe five mils? I think that's the line on the cup. Last night and again this morning for the ear.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else lately?

[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We did one dose of that purple kids' cough syrup, I can't remember the name, the bottle's just purple, and I stopped it. He was bouncing off the walls. And back in January urgent care sent cefdinir and we never picked it up, never gave a drop.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicine allergies?
[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um. Amoxicillin, long ago. He got a rash, maybe. I'm not sure it was from that.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): When, and what kind of rash?

[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I can't pin the date. He was still a baby, under one, could've been longer ago than that. Little red spots? Or it was just a drool rash. My sister was the one who freaked out, I barely remember.
[SEG0036] person_4 (PATIENT): No no!
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any surgeries? Ear infections before this?
[SEG0038] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No surgeries. First time his ear's done this.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): I need to look. Hold his head.
[SEG0040] person_4 (PATIENT): Stop! Ow!
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right eardrum is pink, I can still see the landmarks, no hole, no pus. Left ear looks normal. Throat's a bit red. Neck isn't swollen. Lungs are clear.
[SEG0042] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So is it infected?
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): It might be an early ear infection, or it might just be fluid and pressure after the cold. I can't say which for certain today.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): We're going to watch it. Keep using the Tylenol for pain, you can switch to ibuprofen if you want, the berry children's one is fine. No antibiotic starting today.
[SEG0045] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We have that berry Motrin at home. I haven't opened it this week.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Because of that maybe-amoxicillin rash I'm not using amoxicillin. I'll send cefdinir suspension to your pharmacy, one hundred twenty-five milligrams per five mils, eight mils by mouth once a day for five days. Don't fill it unless he's still miserable tomorrow night or he gets a real fever.
[SEG0047] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. That's the one we never used before, yeah.
[SEG0048] person_4 (PATIENT): Home.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): If he's not turning the corner in two days, or sooner if he spikes a fever or the ear starts draining, come back. Otherwise you don't need another visit.
[SEG0050] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What if he just cries tonight again?
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain medicine, fluids, and if you're worried he's worse, call us. Don't start the cefdinir just for one more fussy night.
[SEG0052] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Alright. He's usually a terror in the car, so, fun drive home in this rain.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Drive safe. We're done.
[SEG0054] person_4 (PATIENT): Bye. Ear.
[SEG0055] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks. Come on, Leo.
